fields.title: 1. Event — Source Cross-Check of Two DoD OSC Conditional Loan Commitments
fields.md:
### 1-1. Original Text and Reprints (③ Government Announcement)

| Item | Stoke Space | Rocket Lab | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Announcement date | 2026-10-26 (Mon) | 2026-11-09 (Mon) | Stoke: ⑤ [Air & Space Forces 10/27](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/pentagon-finance-second-launch-pad-stoke-space/) · Rocket Lab: ⑤ [Defense Daily 11/10](https://www.defensedaily.com/rocket-lab-gets-150-million-conditional-loan-commitment-from-pentagon-osc-for-neutron/space/) |
| Amount | Conditional loan commitment of $150 million | Conditional loan commitment of $150 million | Same · ③ [war.gov press release 4644766](https://www.war.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/4644766/the-department-of-wars-office-of-strategic-capital-signs-150-million-conditiona/) (tool returned 403 — reprint [newsroomamerica 11/9](https://newsroomamerica.com/a/XPzzHNEmZrBRHVkdtE1DtF1Hmap/the_office_of_strategic_capital_has_signed_a_150_million_conditional_loan_commitment_with_rocket_lab_to_boost_flight_rates_of_its_reusable_neutron_rocket_and_expand_us_launch_capacity.html), attributed to Department of War) |
| Use | A **second launch pad** next to the existing complex at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station — Nova Block 2 (fully reusable, 15-ton class to low Earth orbit) · paired with private capital | Expanding flight cadence **after Neutron's first launch** — accelerating vehicle delivery and processing, recovery and transport vessels, composite and engine production facilities, turnaround infrastructure between launches | Same |
| Conditions | Not final until financial, legal and technical requirements are met | Financial, legal, technical, investment and due-diligence stages before financial close | Same |
| What was **not disclosed** | Interest rate · maturity · total pad cost · construction start date | Interest rate · maturity (per the announcement) | Same |
| Vehicle status | Nova Pathfinder first flight expected early 2027 · Block 2 first flight expected 2029 — both pre-flight | Neutron first flight targeted for 2027 — pre-flight | ⑤ Air & Space Forces 10/27 · ⑥ [mlq.ai](https://mlq.ai/news/pentagon-offers-rocket-lab-a-150-million-loan-to-speed-up-neutron-as-spacex-winds-down-falcon-9/) (title only, body 403) |

### 1-2. Differences Between Reports and the Original

| Statement | Source | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| '$300 million conditional loan' | ⑥ mezha.net · mlq.ai (detected by the watcher) | **Combined figure** — not a single program but two separate commitments two weeks apart (150 + 150 = 300). Each original is $150 million (source: table 1-1) |
| LeoLabs $150 million from the same office's OSC (space surveillance radar, up to $300 million including private co-investment) | ⑥ [SatNews 11/5](https://satnews.com/2026/11/05/pentagon-commits-150m-osc-loan-to-leolabs-in-300m-radar-network-expansion/) · [Air & Space Forces](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/pentagon-loans-150m-to-leolabs-to-build-ground-radars/) | **A different event** — not a launch. It happens to be the same number as the headline's $300 million, so we do not mix them |
| 'As SpaceX winds down Falcon 9' · halt of Falcon 9 commercial bookings after 2028 | ⑤ Reprints of the original September reports by Bloomberg and Ars Technica (⑥ [TechSpot](https://www.techspot.com/news/113977-spacex-may-stop-flying-falcon-9-after-2028.html) and others) | **Unconfirmed** — no retirement schedule in SpaceX filings or IR. The scope also differs by report (dedicated commercial launches only · including rideshare · some government missions retained until 2030). Not used in the verdict |
| Space Force concerned about launch bottlenecks from Falcon 9 retirement | ⑤ Air & Space Forces 10/27 (Space Force Col. Zarynisky: regularly discusses future plans with NSSL providers) | Context record only — the OSC announcement itself says only 'expanding U.S. launch capacity to meet growing commercial and national security demand' |

### 1-3. Filings and Company Materials

- **No SpaceX 8-K or IR** — the latest on EDGAR is still the 11/06 8-K (Item 5.02, accn 0001628280-26-071689) (source: ① [EDGAR filing list](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json), checked afternoon of 2026-11-11).
- Rocket Lab was added to NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 with Neutron in 2025-03 (company announcement — source: [Scoop reprint 2025-03](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/SC2503/S00061.htm)). This loan is an investment in supply capacity, not a contract award.

**Verdict**: The event is **real** (government announcement, cross-checked by top-tier reports) — but none of it touches SpaceX's numbers. There are two paths, and both take time.

1. **Axis E (E-2027-4 new federal contract awards at or above prior year)**: The government funding an alternative to SpaceX supply is the opposite end of the 'government dependence' debate — its direction overlaps with the CEO's 11/6 remark that 'government revenue will fall below 10% of the total' (candidate table). But NSSL assignments cannot change before the two vehicles fly. The E-2027-4 verdict rests only on amounts in USAspending and DoD contract announcements (source: `state.milestones` E-2027-4 · table 1-1).
2. **Axis B (launch business)**: If the halt of Falcon 9 commercial bookings is true, competitors would be entering a market SpaceX is vacating itself, not taking it away. Which it is will be told by the launch business description and risk factors in the 4Q26 10-K — for now there are only reports (source: table 1-2 · T13 check).

**Measurement-layer items (listing only)**: ① The watcher could not link this event to any trigger — there was no trigger of the 'competing launch provider funding / government supply policy' type (newly created as T13 in this run). ② The measurement layer's competing-launch monitoring only searches the names Amazon Leo and New Glenn — the first flights of Neutron and Nova are outside monitoring (source: CLAUDE.md detection mapping table · `state.open_questions_for_next_run`).
